gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a driver-free dual extender needs one native video connection per added screen, as FOPO puts it for the S1: 'Each S1 screen needs its own supported video connection'. So on an M1 or M2 MacBook Air, or an M3 Air with its lid open, which Apple specs at one external display, only one of the two screens lights. A single-cable hub (MST) does not get around this, because Plugable states 'MST is not supported on macOS for extended displays'. The M5 MacBook Air drives two.
standout_why: Pages compared: itechguides 15 Best (2026), cited; rottenwifi 15 Best (2026), cited; theofficejournal Best Laptop Screen Extenders; deskfinds under-$300 (returned HTTP 403, not read). itechguides and rottenwifi cover DisplayPort Alt Mode against DisplayLink in general terms. rottenwifi says 'Do not assume every MacBook supports two or three independent external displays', and both say a second screen can stay blank. None of them names MST or says it mirrors on macOS. None gives a display count per MacBook chip, and none says a driver-free dual extender needs one video connection per screen. theofficejournal covers only Alt Mode, HDMI and USB-A power. ChatGPT's own answer warned that some base Apple Silicon MacBooks support one monitor, so part of the idea is already in front of the shopper. That is why this scores 2, not 3. What's new is the rule of one connection per screen, the exact limit for each chip, and the fact that a single cable can't get around it on a Mac.
decides: This splits the pick by laptop. On an M1 or M2 MacBook Air, or an M3 Air used with the lid open, a driver-free dual extender under $300 (FOPO S1, FOPO S7, or the dual UPERFECT/AOKER in the chats) lights only one of its screens. That makes the single-screen Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS the honest pick there: its USB-C/mini-HDMI input needs no driver and uses the one display the Mac has. For a Windows laptop with two video-capable USB-C ports (or USB-C plus HDMI), or an M4 or M5 MacBook, the FOPO S1 or S7 dual wins the two-extra-screens segment under $300. Getting three screens on a base M1–M3 Air needs a driver-based (DisplayLink-type) extender. The one in our records, the FOPO S788, is over budget.
